dedupe_keys.name: blue spot flood screening of national road networks in denmark sweden and the netherlands

description: This Climate-ADAPT tool page documents the Blue Spot model and its application by three national road authorities. A blue spot is a stretch of road where flooding is relatively likely and its consequences are significant. The method runs in a GIS on digital terrain models with hydrological corrections, precipitation statistics and climate factors, soil information, demography and traffic loads, in three levels: terrain screening of local depressions, precipitation sensitivity of depression capacity, and hydrodynamic modelling of surface reservoirs. It was developed in the SWAMP project led by the Danish Road Institute and first applied by the Danish Road Directorate to the national road network, for present conditions and for 2050 and 2100 under IPCC scenarios. The Swedish Transport Administration then screened TEN-T road sections in southern Sweden for extreme daily precipitation up to 2100, and Rijkswaterstaat had Deltares identify flood-prone spots on the Dutch national highway network, with flood probabilities now and in 2050. The page, from 2016 and updated in 2023, is accessible online as free HTML with links to a Nordic Roads article and the TRID record. Caveats: no software is published, the page gives no counts or maps of blue spots found, and results depend on terrain model resolution. The case illustrates hazard exposure screening and climate adaptation of road networks to pluvial flooding; related records are the Netherlands national road network (NWB) and the Holdfast Bay road corridor study.
name: Blue Spot flood screening of national road networks in Denmark, Sweden and the Netherlands
outcomes: Flood-prone road stretches were identified on the Danish national roads (now, 2050 and 2100), on TEN-T roads in southern Sweden and on the Dutch national highway network, with flood probabilities for now and 2050.
provider: Climate-ADAPT (European Environment Agency), tool page on the Blue Spot model from the SWAMP project

sources.note: Climate-ADAPT tool record: definition, input data, three levels, SWAMP project TR081, Danish, Swedish and Dutch applications; published 2016-06-07, modified 2023-12-12
